title: Logger framework design
idea: A logger framework lets code report events by level, then decides separately which events to keep, how to format them and where to write them.
points: `Logger` checks the level first, so a dropped message costs almost nothing.
A log record is plain data: time, level, logger name and message.
A formatter turns a record into text, such as plain lines or JSON.
Appenders are destinations; adding a file or network target means one new class.

hero.title: One log call, start to finish

steps.caption: Application code calls `log.info` and knows nothing about files, consoles or formats.
The logger compares INFO with its minimum level. INFO passes.
The logger builds one record, reading the time from an injected clock.
Each appender asks its own formatter to turn the record into a line.
Every appender writes the line to its own destination: here the console and a memory list.
A `debug` call arrives while the minimum level is INFO.
The level check fails. No record is built and no appender runs.

code.title: Levels are numbers
code.caption: A level filter is one comparison. Change `'WARN'` to `'DEBUG'` and run again.

code.title: Logger, formatters, appenders
code.caption: Two appenders, two formats, one call site. Add a `WarnOnlyAppender` that ignores anything below WARN.

walk.text: Levels map to numbers, so filtering is a simple comparison.
Formatters decide how a record looks. Both share one `format(record)` method.
Appenders decide where a line goes. Each one is given its formatter.
`Logger` receives its level, appenders and clock instead of creating them.
Filter first, build the record once, then hand it to every appender.
Wiring happens in one place. A fixed clock keeps the output repeatable.
The debug line is dropped; the other three reach both appenders.

pitfalls: Do not build costly messages before the level check; pass cheap values or check first.
Never log passwords, tokens or card numbers; mask them before the record is built.
Do not call `new Date()` inside the logger; inject a clock so tests can assert lines.

quiz.why: Only levels at or above 30 pass. `filter` keeps the array's own order, so ERROR comes before WARN.

takeaway: Filter by level, then format and write through swappable appenders.

starters: Should a logger be a Singleton or passed in with dependency injection?
